nav.footer: Local vision. Explicit rules. Inspectable evidence.
nav.reference: Detailed technical references and the video lab are currently in English.

home.lead: A Python library for visible people counting, dwell rules and reproducible event evidence. Run locally on CPU or NVIDIA, with no ongoing LLM calls.
home.install_note: Install from the downloaded checkout. Not published to PyPI.
home.preview_label: ACTUAL MODEL OUTPUT / NORMAL PRODUCT HANDLING
home.preview_title: A box becomes a track. A track supports a rule.
home.preview_body: This local run produced one dwell event after three supported seconds. The lab lets you inspect the detections, timer resets and mistakes across all three models.
home.preview_credit: Footage: Gustavo Fring / Pexels. Normal activity; no criminal allegation or endorsement.
home.proof_body: Recorded software tests, model execution and sparse count checks establish different things. The difficult clips expose false detections and fragmented identities. They do not establish theft recognition or production camera accuracy.
home.cap_count_body: Count eligible confirmed tracks inside a normalized polygon. Unknown coverage stays distinct from an empty scene.
home.cap_dwell_body: Measure one observed track episode. Missing tracks, source gaps and epoch changes reset the timer instead of inventing continued presence.
home.cap_replay_body: Save observations, configuration and hashes. Reproduce rule events and inspect the evidence that caused them.
home.flow_title: Separate perception from the meaning you assign.
home.flow_detect_body: Local ONNX adapters use each model's explicit preprocessing and class map.
home.flow_track_body: The baseline associates overlapping boxes and confirms temporary identities.
home.flow_rule_body: Typed configuration applies count and dwell rules to timestamped observations.
home.flow_evidence_body: Counts, events and replay artifacts retain the source, track and supported interval.
home.flow_note: The standard-library core can also consume observations from your own detector and tracker.
home.quick_title: One small example. Every output explained.
home.quick_text: Begin with synthetic observation replay, then add the vision dependencies and local model artifacts for video.
home.quick_output: The demo writes 41 count samples and one dwell event. Inspect events.jsonl, counts.jsonl and summary.json.
home.hardware_intel_body: CPU-only ONNX execution, automated tests and learned-model regressions were run on the recorded Intel host.
home.hardware_nvidia_body: All three shortlisted models ran with separately profiled CUDA kernel execution on an RTX 5060 Ti.
home.hardware_amd_body: CPU fixture integration passed on AMD GitHub runners. Full learned-model qualification remains pending.
home.hardware_apple_body: CPU integration and a tiny CoreML fixture passed on a GitHub M1 virtual runner. Full learned-model qualification remains pending.
home.repos_title: Source code, model contracts and upstream repositories.
home.repos_text: The library source, README and roadmap are public on GitHub. The upstream projects below are separate repositories.
home.repos_own_body: Library, tests, examples, documentation and recorded evidence. Model weights and demo media are prepared separately.
home.repos_all: Browse all source and license details
home.repo_rtmdet: The RTMDet-Tiny model family and its MMDetection export environment.
home.repo_dfine: The D-FINE-N COCO checkpoint and deployed output contract.
home.repo_rf: The RF-DETR-Nano exporter and model-specific class map.
home.repo_ort: The local inference runtime and its hardware execution providers.
home.research_text: Our research separates existing solutions from narrower opportunities: reliable source-time evidence, tracker-aware rules, camera qualification and reproducible deployment. Proposed work is not presented as a shipped feature.
home.research_link: Explore the evidence and proposed priorities
home.faq_a1: No. Version 0.3 implements visible counting and observed dwell. It has no theft, concealment, payment or ownership classifier. The fictional theft scenes make that boundary visible.
home.faq_q2: Does inference need a cloud API?
home.faq_a2: No. Runtime uses local model artifacts. There are no ongoing LLM calls or automatic model downloads in the processing loop.
home.faq_q3: Can I use the code commercially?
home.faq_a3: The original code is Apache-2.0. Exact weights, datasets, codecs, GPU packages and footage retain their own terms. An ONNX export does not grant new rights.
home.faq_q4: Is this a live camera service?
home.faq_a4: The current runner processes local video files offline. Live RTSP reconnect, stream scheduling and durable alert delivery are not implemented.
home.faq_a5: The home page, navigation and getting-started guide are available in twelve languages. Detailed technical references, research details and the interactive lab currently use English.
home.bottom_text: Install the core, run a replay and inspect its evidence before choosing a model or adding more behaviours.

guide.title: Your first explained event
guide.intro: Use Python 3.12 and a fresh virtual environment. Extract the source archive and run these commands from its root. This prototype is not published to PyPI.
guide.step1_body: The core uses Python's standard library. The synthetic demo exercises counting and dwell without downloading weights or using a GPU.
guide.step2_body: Expect 41 count samples and one dwell event. summary.json must report status: ok. Replaying the same observations reproduces the count and event records.
guide.step3_body: Use one ONNX Runtime distribution per environment. Choose CPU or NVIDIA CUDA; do not combine their extras. Apple Silicon uses the apple extra and native arm64 Python, with physical hardware validation still pending.
guide.step4_body: The three shortlisted models need local ONNX files and manifests. Use a separate export environment and follow the English model-preparation reference. Weights are excluded from the wheel and source ZIP.
guide.step5_body: Edit configs/people.json for the camera's normalized zones. The offline runner saves observations and evaluates the same stream through the rules. Check the selected provider and final summary status.
guide.step6_body: A successful demo or fast inference does not establish camera accuracy. Label real counts and dwell episodes, include occlusions and source gaps, and measure false alerts and missed events.
guide.english_note: The linked technical references are currently in English. Commands and API identifiers remain unchanged in every language.
